# 0.1.24 — Cursor and Grok Bot can connect

- **Cursor on the web, Cursor Cloud Agents and Grok Bot can sign in.** Their callback `https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback` is now built in, so an update enables it without editing Worker variables.
- **Cursor desktop app.** It registers that callback together with `http://localhost:8787/callback`, so it also needs **Allow AI apps on this computer** under **AI connections**, like Claude Code.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.23 — Antigravity stays connected

- **No more failing background stream.** MCP clients may open a background event stream with a GET request. Publisher has no such stream, but it answered with one and closed it at once, so clients retried. Antigravity gave up after five tries and marked Publisher as failed ("standalone SSE stream: exceeded 5 retries without progress"), even though sign-in and tools worked. Publisher now answers `405 Method Not Allowed`, which tells clients there is no stream. ChatGPT, Claude and other clients already handle this.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.22 — Muse can use the tools

- **Muse's tool calls are accepted.** Publisher refused every MCP request that carried an `Origin` header from another site with `403 Unexpected origin`, before checking the sign-in. Muse sends one, so it could connect but not list or call tools. The MCP endpoint now accepts any `Origin`, because it only accepts access tokens, never browser cookies. The control panel and sign-in pages still refuse requests from other sites.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.21 — Muse sign-in fix

- **Muse can finish connecting.** After you press **Allow project access**, Publisher now shows a short "Returning to your AI client" page that forwards the browser to the AI client, instead of redirecting straight away. Muse's callback forwards again to a second address (agent.meta.ai → muse.ai), and the browser blocked that second hop after the approval form. Muse never got its sign-in code, and pressing Allow again showed "This authorization was not started in this browser". ChatGPT, Claude and other clients work as before.
- **Leftover Muse entries.** Each blocked attempt still created an entry under **AI connections → Connected apps** ("not used yet"). Revoke those, then connect again from Muse.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.20 — Antigravity and Muse can connect

- **Google Antigravity and Meta Muse can sign in.** Their callbacks `https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback` and `https://agent.meta.ai/api/hatch/oauth/callback` are now built in, next to ChatGPT and Claude, so an update enables them without editing Worker variables. Callbacks stay exactly allowlisted and PKCE S256 stays required.
- **Settings.** The Cloudflare settings panel is now called **Settings**.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.19 — Tweak cockpit wording

- Better wording in Publisher cockpit

# 0.1.18 — change your owner password

- **Change owner password.** In **Cloudflare settings → Change owner password**, enter your current password and a new one (12–256 characters). Wrong current passwords count toward the same limit as sign-in: 10 tries per 15 minutes.
- **Everyone else is signed out.** A password change ends every other browser session and revokes every connected AI app, so access shared with someone else (for example a reviewer) ends with the old password. You stay signed in. Reconnect the AI apps you still use.
- **Password recovery also clears AI connections.** Resetting a lost password from the Cloudflare dashboard already blocked existing AI apps; they are now also removed from **AI connections → Connected apps** instead of lingering there.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.17 — release channel with rollback protection

- **Updates without editing Cloudflare settings.** Publishers now follow the release channel `https://publisher.jumpermcp.dev/releases/`, which always serves the newest signed release. **Check for updates** offers each new release; you still review and approve every update. New installations use the channel automatically. To switch an existing installation once, set the Worker variable `RELEASE_BASE_URL` to `https://publisher.jumpermcp.dev/releases/`.
- **No rollbacks from the channel.** The Publisher refuses a channel release older than the one installed. A release host that was taken over can then only withhold updates, not push an old version back. Signatures are checked as before. Pointing `RELEASE_BASE_URL` at a numbered release folder still pins that version on purpose, for recovery.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.16 — upload links for images, ZIPs and large files

- **New tool `create_upload`.** An AI app with a shell or code sandbox, such as Claude Code or Claude with code execution, asks for a one-time upload link and sends the file's bytes there directly (`curl -X PUT --data-binary @FILE …`). It then passes the returned `upload_id` in `uploads` to `stage_project` or `publish_project`. Images, ZIPs and big text files no longer have to pass through the chat, which made them impossible before.
- **Limits.** Each link works once and expires after 10 minutes. A single file can be up to 10 MiB and a ZIP up to 25 MiB, and at most 20 uploads (100 MiB) can wait at a time. Unused uploads are removed after an hour. Uploads only fill a private draft; nothing becomes public without a publish.
- **Clear error instead of a silent no-op.** `file_path` without an attached file used to stage nothing without saying so. It now explains that `create_upload` is the way to send a file.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.15 — Claude sign-in fix and refused sign-in details

- **Claude can register.** Claude.ai registers as a client with a client secret, which 0.1.14 refused ("Couldn't register with … sign-in service"). Apps that return to a hosted callback (ChatGPT, Claude) may now register with or without a secret. Callbacks stay exactly allowlisted, PKCE S256 stays required, and apps on your computer (localhost callbacks) still register without a secret.
- **Last refused sign-in.** When the Publisher refuses an app's registration, AI connections shows what the app sent: its name, callback and client authentication method. Nothing secret is stored.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.14 — Claude connectors and per-app access

- **Claude on the web, Desktop and mobile can connect.** The Claude connector callback `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback` is now built in, next to the ChatGPT callback. Both are part of the code, so an update enables them even when the Worker variables are older than this release.
- **`CHATGPT_CALLBACKS` is renamed `ALLOWED_CALLBACKS`.** It now only adds extra callbacks to the built-in ones. Existing installs keep their `CHATGPT_CALLBACKS` value, and it is still read when `ALLOWED_CALLBACKS` is not set.
- **AI connections panel.** The cockpit panel "ChatGPT connection" is now "AI connections". It lists every connected AI app with where it signs in from, the approval date and the last use, and has a **Revoke** button for each one. Revoking signs out that app only. Resetting the password still signs out all of them.
- **Sign-in from apps on your computer is a cockpit switch.** Claude Code and other local apps sign in through a `localhost` callback. The owner can now turn this on and off under AI connections → AI apps on this computer. The `ALLOW_LOOPBACK_CALLBACKS=true` Worker variable still forces it on.
- **Tool titles.** Every MCP tool now has a human-readable title, which the Claude connector directory requires.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.

# 0.1.13 — opt-in sign-in for local AI clients

The Publisher can now accept sign-in from MCP clients that run on your own computer, such as coding agents in a terminal. These clients receive the sign-in result on a `localhost` address with a changing port. This is off by default. To turn it on, set the text variable `ALLOW_LOOPBACK_CALLBACKS` to `true` in the Publisher Worker's Cloudflare settings (Settings → Variables and Secrets). Publisher updates keep this setting.

When it is on, loopback callbacks (`http://localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, any port) are accepted at registration, on the approval page and at approval. The rules are unchanged otherwise: public client, PKCE S256, and no credentials, query or fragment in the callback. When it is off, such a client is refused with a message naming the setting. For a local callback, the approval page warns that any program on that computer can open it, so approve only a sign-in you just started yourself. The approval page now says "your AI client" instead of ChatGPT. The configured ChatGPT callback is unchanged.

No migration, credential, or origin changes.
